Legal research is otherwise complete and would support a YES claim: Section 1 and Section 2 operative; EO 12608 section 2 (1987-09-09) is the only amendment; Code note under 42 U.S.C. 2652 prints the order as amended.

Section 2(a) of EO 11085 amends section 4 of EO 10717 (members of the Distinguished Civilian Service Awards Board serve at the pleasure of the President) and says the other sections of EO 10717 are amended conformably. EO 12014 (1977-10-19, held) abolished the Board and deleted sections 3 to 9 of EO 10717, which ends the section 4 amendment, but the text of EO 10717 before and after EO 11085 is not held in the packet, so it cannot be shown whether any conforming amendment to the surviving sections 1 and 2 of EO 10717 continues. Missing: the 1957 and 1961 texts of EO 10717 (22 FR 4632; 26 FR 11937) to identify the conforming changes, or a source stating them. Without it clause 2(a) has no supportable first end.

The dossier's clause boundaries also need an inventory correction before a claim can be assembled: its first clause spans the whole restated text of EO 9586 sections 1 to 5 (chars 714-3728) and its second spans 3(c) to 6; the correct units are restated sections 1, 2(a)-(d), 3, 4, 5 and 6 (sections 3-6 struck by EO 11515 section 5(2), 1970-03-13) plus sections 2(a) and 2(b) of EO 11085 itself.

Legal reading from held evidence (not submitted): the order's operative text in EO 9586 sections 1 and 2 (medal established; award by the President; 2(b) replaced by EO 11515) remains in force; no revocation is held. Every CURRENT record for this order is custody-record-only (Code bytes not held), so a current predicate would have to rest on the original plus bounded searches.

Section 1 delegates 'the authority vested in the President by section 271 of title 10'. Former 10 U.S.C. 271 no longer exists under that number; the held Code note prints the order under 10 U.S.C. 10149 with the editorial bracket [see 10149]. The text of 10 U.S.C. 10149 as in force on 2026-10-14, and the restatement act showing that the former section 271 authority to prescribe screening regulations passed to it, are not held (jobs/current-law/output/usc-sections holds no title 10 section 271 or 10149 text). Per the producer rule for orders whose authority statute was renumbered or repealed, a YES claim is blocked until that statute text is held.

Otherwise the order reads as in force: Section 2 (revoking EO 10651) took effect on issuance; EO 11382 section 13 and EO 13286 section 67 changed only the Coast Guard officer named; no revocation held; DoD rule 64 FR 72027 (1999) cites 10 U.S.C. 10149 and EO 11190 together.
